articleTitle: Dielectric Object Subsurface Survey by Ultrawideband Radar and ANN
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of subsurface object classification by ground penetrating radar with artificial neural network data processing is solving in the work. Antenna system generates ultrashort impulse electromagnetic field and receive the reflections from the investigated area of ground. Obtained signals are exempted from surface influence and normalized on the root of its energy for amplifying the useful part of the impulse. Neural network implements the detection of the objects in the angular sector relatively to antenna system. Asymmetrical dielectric mine response on impulse electromagnetic wave is calculated in two spatial positions for obtaining better results of its detection by artificial neural network. Recognition results are presented in the form of radar display. The neural network is tested on the intermediate positions of the mine from the reference training data. Approximation properties of the artificial neural network are investigated.

articleTitle: Time and Space Properties of Signals of Non-Contact Ultrasonic Testing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The system of non-contact ultrasonic testing of polymer composite materials by the through-transmission method system is described. Envelopes of fundamental and higher harmonics are investigated by discrete Fourier transformation. The model of ratio of polynomials is used for describing spectra of time signals. The quadrature components are found by modified Prony method. The spatial resolving power is investigated.

articleTitle: Dual-objective Design of Multilayer Radar Absorbing Composite Material Using Butterfly Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A Multilayer Radar Absorbing Material (MRAM) based on composite is designed using a dual-objective optimization method butterfly optimization algorithm (BOA). The two objective functions regard Total Reflection (TR) involving sub-reflection at the inner layers and Total Thickness (TT). In order to make the MRA material more applicable for real applications; first, Mean Oblique Incidence (MOI) of TR in the range of 0-60 degree with polarizations TE/TM and then the average of MOI-TR in the range of 2-18 GHz is taken for achieving MOI-TR<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">avg</sub>. The design variables, i.e. the thickness and material specimens for each layer from a material database including 21 composite specimens is optimally determined for synchronously minimizing the two objectives. Thus, a Global optimum MRAM (GMRAM) is picked out within the distributed candidate optimal solution set through Pareto optimality. Therefore, a five-layer GMRAM effectively absorbing at 7-18 GHz is successfully determined with the objectives of -10.85 dB MOI-TR<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">avg</sub> and 4.2493 mm TT by considering the trade-off between the two objectives. The GMRAM is compared with a respective design in the literature to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed optimization method. The TT is reduced as 66% by keeping the TR performance almost the same thanks to the effective and versatile dual-objective optimization with BOA.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Plane Waveguide Array Based on a Strict Solution of Analysis Problem
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The synthesis problem of plane rectangular waveguide array has been solved using the strict solution of the respective direct electrodynamic problem. The integral equation system of Hallen type is used for determination of the current distribution in the waveguide's apertures. The optimal excitation coefficients in apertures are determined while minimization of functional presenting the mean-square deviation of the given and synthesized amplitude radiation pattern (RP). The additional terms in the functional are applied for the minimization of radiation in a near zone and limitation on the values of excitation coefficients. The computational results demonstrate the ability to synthesize the given amplitude RPs of various types.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Cutoff Wavenumbers of Circular Metallic-Anisotropic Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this work we calculate the cutoff wavenumbers of circular waveguides consisting of a metallic wall and loaded with an inhomogeneous anisotropic medium. The anisotropic material is characterized by a uniaxial or gyroelectric type permittivity, while its permeability equals to that of free space. The technique we apply is based on the extraction of the cutoff wavenumbers thru a determinantal equation, i.e., the characteristic equation of the problem, obtained via a volume integral equation method which utilizes entire domain vectorial basis functions. The method is validated by comparing the volume integral equation results with the separation of variables solution for single-layered isotropic, uniaxial and gyroelectric loaded waveguides, for both TE and TM modes as well as for hybrid HE and EH modes. In addition, we investigate the validity for two-layered isotropic and uniaxial structures by employing the HFSS commercial software. Discussion on the efficiency of the proposed method is also given.

articleTitle: Analytical Numerical Method for Solving Integral Hammerstein Equations Arising in Free Phase Problems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The nonlinear integral equations of Hammerstein type arise in problems with a free phase. A polynomial approach is used to solve such equations. A system of transcendental equations is constructed to find complex parameters (polynomial roots). For more general optimization problems, this system is supplemented by a linear integral equation. For the case of solutions vanishing on the finite interval, a system of integralfunctional equations is obtained. The branching of solutions is investigated.

articleTitle: Mobile Antenna Matching Study Considering Different Holding Positions at 2100 MHz Frequency
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The purpose of the present research is to study mobile phone Dipole antennas' matching to a free space with a variety of human hand (fingers) positions in case of different positions of the human head and the headset; Since the hand, holding the mobile phone, absorbs a big part of emitted energy during EMF exposure process and therefore, affects antenna matching conditions, it was great importance to estimate the SAR values in the human head, and to investigate the dependency between SAR and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> coefficient (antenna matching parameter). The EMF in near and far zones and reradiated power are also studied. Numerical simulation is conducted on realistic nonhomogeneous human head and hand models by the FDTD (Finite Difference Time Domain) Method at 2100 MHz standard frequency.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Force Characteristic of the “Coil-Permanent Magnet” System in the Presence of Ferromagnetic Elements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this article, an integral mathematical model was obtained for calculating the force, which acts on a permanent magnet or ferromagnetic body in systems with axial symmetry. The case of constant currents in the system is considered. This mathematical model can be extended to the presence of alternating currents and the influence of motion on the electromagnetic process. which will be discussed in the following publications. The adequacy of the obtained models is confirmed by comparing the intermediate results with the solution of finite element methods. The obtained simulation results will allow analyzing the distribution of forces acting in the system. and to solve the problems of synthesis of magnetic systems with given characteristics. It is shown that the problem of calculating the components of the magnetic field induction vector in the presence of permanent magnets and ferromagnetic elements can be rather complicated and requires an understanding of the processes occurring in the system.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of the Complex Reflection Coefficient from the Data of Measurements of Scalar Reflectometer in Free Space by a Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The concept of reconstruction of the complex reflection coefficient from the data of measurements with a scalar reflectometer based on frequency-time transformations is considered. Its modification is proposed for the case of free space measurements of longitudinally extended structures by a horn antenna. To improve the efficiency of the approach, it is proposed to use parametric spectral analysis based on the method of quasisolution searching.

articleTitle: Radiation Patterns of Two Coupled Impedance Monopoles Located on Metal Rectangular Screen
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The 3D vector problem of diffraction of the fields of two coupled resonant impedance monopoles placed on an infinitely thin rectangular ideally conducting screen and oriented perpendicularly to it has been solved in frames of the method of the uniform geometric diffraction theory with using the asymptotic for the current in the impedance dipole. As model solution the analytical expression for the pattern of two impedance monopoles, placed on the infinite screen, is obtained and the normalized radiation patterns are analyzed vs. distances between the monopoles. For finite size rectangular screen the analysis of the patterns of total and diffracted fields was carried in the main observation planes and in whole space on the base of developed fast-active algorithm and software. The verification of the numerical results has been made using software Feko. The patterns are in a good agreement.

articleTitle: High Speed Cables Modeling and Simulations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the experimental validation of the modeling approach for studying the shielding cables and their properties for high speed systems. The simulation model is based on the multi-transmission line approach, and the novelty is in special validation of shield structure parameters using measurements of transfer impedance values according to IEC 62153-4-3 [1]. The methodology presented in this paper consists of two steps. Firstly we adjust the shielded structure parameters using measured data and secondly, we assemble radiated emission setup according to CISPR 25 [2] and compare the fields produced by shielded cables with measured data.

articleTitle: Interaction of the Transition Radiation of a Charged Particle with Bi-Periodically Modulated Medium in a Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper is devoted to a theoretical study of the interaction of transition radiation of a moving charged particle with bi-periodically modulated in space dielectric filling of a regular ideal waveguide. We assume that the particle moves at a constant velocity, direction of which is perpendicular to the axis of waveguide. From the system of Maxwell's equations, a wave equations are obtained whose solutions leads to an analytical expressions for the transverse magnetic (TM) and electric (TE) fields of radiation with an accuracy of terms, which is proportional to small modulation depths. It is shown that in this approximation the TM and TE fields in the waveguide are a superposition of spatial harmonics (zero and plus - minus the first harmonics). The energies of the transition radiation of a charged particle in the domain of non-resonant interaction between the radiation and modulation waves of the waveguide filling is calculated (the first-order Wulf-Bragg condition for waves reflected from inhomogeneities of filling is not satisfied). It is shown that the energies of transition radiation at the fundamental (zero) harmonic does not depend on the depths of modulation of the filling, while at the side (plus - minus the first) harmonics they are proportional to the depths of modulation. The Cherenkov radiation frequency is found for the case of a rectangular waveguide.

articleTitle: Cauchy’s Generalized Problem in Solving a Nonlinear Three-parameter Spectral Problem
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper proposes a new numerical method for solving a three-parameter nonlinear spectral problem for holomorphic operator-functions, defined in Banach spaces. The concept of a generalized Cauchy problem is introduced, which is to solve a system of two equations in partial first-order derivatives with a common initial condition. This makes it possible to find connected components of spectrum (CCS) in the form of three-dimensional smooth spectral surfaces.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Combined Monopole-Slot Radiator of Clavin Type
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The ultrawideband monopole-slot radiator is constructed on the base of ultrawideband slot cut in an infinite perfectly conducting screen. To improve directive properties of the slot and to provide effective radiation at low frequencies two monopoles are used similarly to the Clavin radiator construction. Perfectly conducting cones connected to the screen with their bases are used as ultrawideband monopole structures. Optimization process of geometrical parameters of the monopoles is carried out to provide effective interaction between them and ultrawideaband slot. Directivity at different frequencies and time dependences of radiated fields at different angles are presented.

articleTitle: Hybridization of PMCHW Approach with Mitzner Surface Impedance Boundary Conditions for Treating Combined Geometries with Dielectrics and Thin 3D Material Sheets
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper combines the PMCHW approach and Mitzner surface impedance boundary conditions (SIBC) to derive a generalized approach for treating combined geometries, including both dielectric parts and thin 3D material sheets. The developed approach is verified on a number of specific problems by comparison of the results with those obtained by well-known methods and measurements.

articleTitle: Dynamical Consolidation of Cobalt Nanowires for Potential Fabrication of Rare-Earth Free Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Cobalt nanowires were prepared by the electroless deposition method under an applied magnetic field. Their mixtures with copper micropowders polarized under magnetic field were compacted by a hot shock-wave method for production of oriented magnetic nanocomposites for potential rare earth free magnet applications. The magnetic properties of Co nanowire/Cu micropowder composites were studied by simple RF resonant magnetometry and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) measurements with an optical microscopy control of obtained composite one-dimensional nanotextures.

articleTitle: The Substrate Effect on Electrical Characteristics of a Radiator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Electrical characteristics of a radiator placed on a dielectric substrate differ from the characteristics of a similar radiator located in the free space because of capacitance change per unit length of an antenna and a propagation constant of a wave along its axis. The substrate effect was analyzed by means of solving an electrostatic problem for a field of electric charges in the inhomogeneous medium. The problem was solved by the method of a complex potential.

articleTitle: Natural Regularization of the Kernels of Integral Equations for Currents
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The diffraction of electromagnetic waves on a narrow linear slot cut in a bilateral impedance plane is analyzed. The integral equation for surface currents with additive kernel containing Green's functions constructed based on the impedance boundary condition is considered. It was shown by numerical simulation that the Green's functions for this configuration are bounded when source and observation points coincide. Therefore, the equation solution can be obtained without the regularization procedure. Thus, the natural regularization of the integral equation concerning the diffraction problem was substantiated due to using finite values of the surface impedance.

articleTitle: Influence of Ponderomotive Forces of Electromagnetic Waves on Thin Impedance Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A comparative analysis of the ponderomotive effect of a plane wave upon thin scattering impedance dipoles is carried out based on the rigorous solution of the electrodynamic problem. A numerical model of the dipole with distributed constant reactive impedance was created. It was established that the impedance dipoles experience less force of wave pressure under the resonant condition, as compared with perfectly conducting dipoles. For the first time, numerical estimates of the ponderomotive effect on impedance dipoles have confirmed that the level of such influence can be controlled by varying the reactive impedance of the dipole scatterer.

articleTitle: Application of the Generalized Eigenoscillation Method for Solving the Problems of Nanoplasmonics
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The scattering problem on the dielectric body using the generalized method of eigenoscillation (GMEO) is considered. The nonhomogeneous problem is formulated based on the one of variants of GMEO, in which the dielectric permittivity plays a role of eigenvalue. The respective homogeneous problem is solved using the Debay potentials in the different domains of problem. The obtained linear algebraic system is solved effectively by the method of successive approximations. The computational results related to body with coordinate surfaces are discussed.

articleTitle: Diffraction of SH-Waves in Anisotropic Bodies with Cavities
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A method of investigation of the steady oscillations of anisotropic bodies with cavities under anti-plane deformation has been developed. The formulated problem is reduced to an auxiliary problem of the elasticity theory for isotropic material with modified boundary conditions. The auxiliary problem is solved using the integral equation method. The stresses near the cavities of the elliptical shape caused by the harmonic wave for different anisotropic materials have been calculated.

articleTitle: EM Response Study of an Underground Cavity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Paper presents results of computer modeling based study of underground cavity EM response. Spherical cavity's EM response in soil is considered in wide frequency range and different values of soil electrical conductivity. The study is related to the detection abilities of anti-personnel plastic mines by EM exposure.

articleTitle: SH-Wave Diffraction from the Interface Defect
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of the normal transverse shear-wave (SH-wave) diffraction from the semi-infinite interface inhomogeneity (defect) in the rigid junction of the elastic layer and the half-space is solved. The defect is modeled by the surface with mixed boundary conditions. The solution is obtained by the Wiener-Hopf technique. The dependences of the diffracted field on the structure parameters are presented in analytical form. Verification of the obtained solution is presented.

articleTitle: Shape Reconstruction of Three-Dimensional Body at Resonant Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper the method that reconstructs the body shape at resonant frequencies of its inner domain is extended to the case of three dimensions. A scalar acoustic problem of scattering on three-dimensional body is considered. The “measured” scattered patterns, that is, far-field asymptotics, are calculated by an arbitrarily chosen but linear independent set of fields on the body boundary. Body resonant frequencies are determined from the existence condition of the orthogonal complement function. By this function, the Herglotz wave function can be calculated having the sought body boundary among its zero surfaces. The method is tested on model examples and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Some Aspects of the Use of Microwave Technologies in Non-Invasive Biomedical Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The article describes the basics of microwave diagnostics from the point of view of creating a new method for obtaining data to detect pathologies in biological objects, as well as sensors and computational human phantoms for preliminary modeling of experimental equipment.

articleTitle: Dual-element MIMO Inverted-F Antenna for Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this study, a dual-element inverted multiple input multiple output (MIMO) F antenna (IFA) operating at 2.4 GHz band is designed by means of computational electromagnetic for WLAN wireless devices. The shape of IFA element resembles two superimposed E-shaped strips. IFA element with a small size of 10×13mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> operates at the frequency range of 2.28-2.62 GHz. They are orthogonally placed at the corners of a 50×100mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> main ground board for reducing the mutual coupling, i.e. correlation between the two elements. The radiation and isolation performance of MIMOIFA is examined in regards to the radiation patterns, envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and peak gain. The proposed MIMO-IFA shows quasi-omni-directional pattern, under 0.05 ECC and about 2.7 dBi peak gain at 2.4 GHz. Therefore, it is a better and cheap candidate for 2.4 GHz industrial scientific medical (ISM) band including WLAN as well as wireless mobile devices.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Integral Equations for Multi-Input Radiating Structures
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The need to analyze nonlinear effects arising in the transmitting subsystems of microwave wireless power transmission (WPT) systems, which significantly affect the electromagnetic compatibility and the functioning quality is substantiated. The method of integral equations is proposed for a complete analysis of the problem.Nonlinear integral equations for multi-input radiating structures consisting of radiators with distributed nonlinearity were derived for the steady-state periodic or quasi-periodic operating modes. These equations represent a nonlinear integral equation system for amplitudes of complex current densities distributed on surfaces of the radiators under an assumption of their multimode excitation.

articleTitle: EM Wave Scattering on the Non-Planar Structures with Embedded Set of Micro Inclusions
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The electromagnetic (EM) scattering characteristics are studied for the planar non-coordinate inhomogeneous structures embedded by series of small-size impedance inclusions. The distance between the neighboring particles counts several its diameters, and the density of inclusions is prescribed by the specific law. The explicit formula for the EM field components is reduced. The characteristics of convergence of the build iterative procedure to obtain the auxiliary components of the EM field are studied, and dependence of scattering characteristics on the geometry of inclusions is presented.

articleTitle: Rayleigh Wave Diffraction on Surface Elastic Inclusion in the Half-Space
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The diffraction of the Rayleigh wave on a half-circular elastic inclusion which is located perpendicular to the half-space surface is considered. The low-frequency oscillations spectrum is analyzed. Using the method of boundary integral equations (BIE), the problem is reduced to the integral equations with respect to unknown defect opening functions. The mode-I stress intensity factors as functions of angular coordinate of an inclusion front point and wave number for various relations between the materials parameters are computed.

articleTitle: Agarose Gel and Salt Solution Conductivity Study in Phantom Preparation for mNP Hyperthermia Research
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Electric conductivities are measured and reported for Agarose - salt solutions at magnetic Nano Particles (mNP) hyperthermia applicably frequencies between 50 kHz and 250 kHz.

articleTitle: Effective Models for Metallic Inclusions in Piezoelectric Medium
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A mathematical model of dynamic behavior of a thin metallic inclusion or layer in a piezoelectric medium subjected to longitudinal shear load is constructed. Perfect mechanical contact and zero electric potential are prescribe at the boundary of inclusion. Modeling is performed using the apparatus of the theory of singular perturbations.

articleTitle: Poynting Method and Antenna Radiation Resistance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An analytical method is proposed for determining the radiation resistance of a linear metal radiator. The method is based on using of the Poynting vector. The obtained results are compared with the results of solving the integral equation for a current in an antenna. The method is generalized to the case of radiators with nonzero boundary conditions. Calculation results are given.

abstract: Proceedings of 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED). Tbilisi State University, Tbilisi, Georgia, 2020, 180 p. The Proceedings contain the papers of XXVth International Seminar/Workshop DIPED-2020. The topics of papers include propagation of electromagnetic waves and signals in nonhomogeneous media, antenna synthesis, inverse problems, application of electromagnetic fields, analytical and numerical methods in the electrodynamics and acoustics. For the scientists and engineers in the areas of theoretical and applied electrodynamics, antenna theory and techniques, telecommunications, radio engineering and acoustics.

articleTitle: Condolences from the Georgian Colleagues Remembering Prof. Nikolai Voitovich
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: With great sorrow, we write this memoriam for Prof., D.Sc. Nikolai Nikolayevich Voitovich, who passed away on July 11, 2020. This mournful event is a great loss for all scientists working in the field of electrodynamics, especially for his colleagues, students and friends in various countries. Prof. N. N. Voitovich was an outstanding scientist and pedagogue, who stood at the origins of electrodynamics and mathematical physics and who made an invaluable contribution into diffraction scattering, wave propagation, theory of oscillations, spectra, resonance systems, as well as their application to new objects, such as nanoplasmonics. Prof. N. N. Voitovich was an organizer and chairman of the IEEE Ukraine Section (West) MTT/ED/AP/EP/SSC Societies Joint Chapter, and organizer and permanent participator of the International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave (DIPED).

articleTitle: Dedication to the Memory of Prof. Nikolai Voitovich
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE XXVth International Seminar/Workshop Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper is dedicated to the memory of an outstanding Ukrainian scientist in the field of electrodynamics, wave propagation, theory of antenna synthesis, and non-classical inverse problems, the organizer of the International Seminar/Workshop DIPED and the first IEEE Chapter in Ukraine, a wonderful person, Prof. Nikolai N. Voitovich.
